fields.name: target_visits
fields.description: Initialize to 0 when memory is empty. Let N be the repetition count in the instruction. If the carried-in count is below 2N, the next uncounted target is right for an even count and left for an odd count. Increment once when this cycle shows the instructed cube held above that target at TCP height approximately 0.10 m, with the target activated red. Use the current endpoint and motion frames to confirm arrival; an activation on the other side is not a new visit. Otherwise retain the count, including during release and button operations. Never increment merely because a waypoint is being issued, and never increment on a zero-step unchanged cycle. e.g. 2
fields.annotation: Number of completed, ordered target visits while holding the instructed cube. Start at 0. Count arrivals in the order right, left, right, left, up to twice the requested repetition count. A visit is completed when the carried cube arrives above the corresponding target at TCP height approximately 0.10 m and that target activates red. Record the increment at the cycle showing that arrival, not at the cycle commanding it. Do not count repeated frames of an activation, pickup, release, or button operations. Retain the final count thereafter. Thus all episodes have 0 at cycles 1–4; subsequent arrival cycles have 1, 2, 3, 4, and, for three repetitions, 5, 6. e.g. 2

action:
Start with empty memory, an open hand, and target_visits initialized to zero. Read the cube color and repetition count N from the instruction. Update target_visits from observed arrivals before selecting the action; do not anticipate completion of the action you are about to issue. Right means smaller world y, appearing on the left of the front image; left means larger world y. Locate the two circular targets, the instructed cube, and the gray button on its square base using the calibrated images. Convert image locations to world coordinates using their appropriate surface heights, rather than treating image displacement as world displacement. Use the wrist view for fine localization. Target centers lie essentially on the tabletop; account for the cube's height when estimating its center and for the button's raised surface when localizing it. Do not reuse coordinates from another episode.

When target_visits is zero and the instructed cube is not held, approach vertically above its center at z=0.15 m, gripper open, with roll approximately pi, pitch zero and yaw aligned to its square edges. If already above it at that height, descend to its center at z=0.02 m and close. A grasp is evidenced by the cube between the fingers and finger positions approximately 0.018–0.019 m, rather than an empty fully closed hand. When the newly grasped cube is still low, lift vertically to z=0.15 m, maintaining the grasp and cube-aligned orientation.

When holding the cube clear of the table and target_visits is less than 2N, command the center of the next required target at z=0.10 m: right if target_visits is even, left if odd. Keep the gripper closed and preserve the current orientation. Move directly between target centers at this height; do not lower onto the table, release, return to the pickup position, or insert a lift between visits. A confirmed red activation counts as arrival despite ordinary TCP tracking error; do not demand exact coincidence with the commanded coordinates. If the required target has not activated and arrival is uncertain, refine its center from visible geometry and complete that same visit rather than skipping it.

When target_visits equals 2N and the cube is still held at the final left target, lower at the current TCP x,y to z=0.07 m and open. When the cube has been released and the open hand remains low there, retreat vertically to approximately z=0.15 m while staying open. When the released cube is on the final target and the hand is clear, move above the button center at z=0.15 m, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, yaw=0, gripper open. When already above the button with an open hand, close the empty gripper at the button's nominal approach position. Ensure at least 2 mm of positional motion; if that nominal position is too close to the reported TCP, add a 5 mm upward displacement. When above the button with the empty gripper closed, descend at the button center to commanded z=0.0075 m, retaining the closed gripper and downward orientation. Physical button contact may stop the actual TCP around z=0.024–0.025 m; when the cycle shows this low contact after the descent, retract above the same button to z=0.15 m with the gripper closed, rather than repeatedly pressing downward.

For an ambiguous or otherwise unmatched situation, use current images and gripper state to recover the applicable geometric condition: refine alignment, or raise vertically to safe clearance if low and obstructed. Preserve a held cube and the visit count. Do not invent completed visits or restart the alternating sequence. Never issue an identical-pose action, and do not wait without an observable task-related purpose.
